cards.explanation: The answer is Aaron. Verse 1 says they make the garments "…as well as the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:1) Aaron gets his own wardrobe, friends, and I got a hat and an apron.

The answer is False. The text says they made the garments "…just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:1) That's the plan they follow, start to finish. No workers deciding the fringe needs a little extra something.

The answer is that they hammer the gold thin and cut threads. Verse 3 says, "They hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut threads from them to interweave with the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen…" (Exodus 39:3) Gold thread, y'all. The text calls it the work of a skilled craftsman, and I believe it.

The answer is True. Verse 5 says the waistband "…was of one piece with the ephod, of the same workmanship…" (Exodus 39:5) No stitching on a separate belt later, friends. It's all one piece, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

The answer is the names of the sons of Israel. The stones were "…engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel." (Exodus 39:6) Names, carved in onyx and set in gold. That's some careful handwriting.

The answer is memorial. Verse 7 says they fastened the stones on the shoulder pieces "…as memorial stones for the sons of Israel…" (Exodus 39:7) So the names sit right up on the shoulders of the ephod. The text doesn't say more than that, so I'll leave it right there.

The answer is True. Verse 8 says, "He made the breastpiece with the same workmanship as the ephod, with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen." (Exodus 39:8) Same fancy materials, same workmanship. It's like a batch where every cookie got the same careful stamp.

The answer is the name of one of the tribes. Verse 14 says each stone "…was engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes." (Exodus 39:14) Twelve stones, twelve names, one each, friends. Nobody gets two and nobody gets left out.

The answer is so it won't swing out from the ephod. Verse 21 says they tied the rings together with blue cord "…so that the breastpiece was above the waistband of the ephod and would not swing out from the ephod…" (Exodus 39:21) It stays put, right where it belongs.

The answer is blue. Verse 22 says, "They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth, the work of a weaver…" (Exodus 39:22) One color, all the way through. The verse calls it a weaver's work, start to finish.

The answer is so the opening won't tear. Verse 23 says there was "…a collar around the opening so that it would not tear." (Exodus 39:23) A little reinforcement, and it's a smart one. I've torn a few things by pulling too hard, so I get it.

The answer is bells. Verse 25 says, "They also made bells of pure gold and attached them around the hem between the pomegranates…" (Exodus 39:25) They alternate with the pomegranates around the hem (Exodus 39:26). Bell, pomegranate, bell, pomegranate, friends. That's a pattern I could stamp in my sleep.

The answer is False. The text says "For Aaron and his sons they made tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver…" (Exodus 39:27) So the tunics aren't for Aaron alone, because his sons are included. Verse 41 backs that up with garments "…for his sons to serve as priests."

The answer is HOLY TO THE LORD. Verse 30 says they engraved on the plate, "…like an inscription on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD." (Exodus 39:30) Pure gold, with those words on it. Big message, small plate.

The answer is the turban. Verse 31 says, "Then they fastened to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban, just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:31) Blue cord, gold plate, turban. All set, friends.

The answer is True, and look at that finish! The crown's plate gets its blue cord in verse 31. Then verse 32 says, "So all the work for the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed." (Exodus 39:32) That's the whole to-do list, done. I haven't finished a to-do list since my junk drawer days, and nobody was even assigning me one then.

The answer is that he blesses them. Verse 43 says Moses "…inspected all the work and saw that they had accomplished it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them." (Exodus 39:43) He looked over all of it first, friends. Then he blessed them. I'd be sweating over my own cookie tray during an inspection like that.
